title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models Boost Counterfactual MPC

### The Breakthrough
AD-WM adds a residual latent dynamics component plus an inverse‑dynamics‑based action‑recovery regularizer to a joint‑embedding world model, preserving action information and raising hard‑start success from 3.7% to 52% and zero‑shot pick‑and‑place on a real Franka arm from 42.2% to 71%.

### The Caveats
The real‑world validation is limited to a single basic pick‑and‑place on a Franka arm, so broader claims remain unproven.

## Rolling-WAM: Faster World-Action Models via Rolling Imagination

### The Breakthrough
Rolling‑WAM keeps a sliding window of video‑action chunks with a rolling noise schedule that fully denoises the imminent chunk while partially refining future ones, delivering a reported 4.5× steady‑state replanning speedup while keeping performance, demonstrated on simulation benchmarks and a real Unitree G1 humanoid.

### The Caveats
Speedup and performance are only benchmarked against a single baseline (standard joint WAMs).

## Contact as Decision Variable: Capability-Tradeoff Contact Selection

### The Breakthrough
CTCS screens candidate contacts, predicts their capabilities via local sensitivity analysis, and selectively performs exact whole‑body optimizations, achieving about a 3× speedup over exhaustive evaluation while preserving objective values, shown on a Unitree Go2 quadruped with an AgileX NERO arm.

### The Caveats
Demonstrated only on a single quadruped‑arm platform in quasi‑static tasks.

## RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations

### The Breakthrough
RAPID infers task specifications, action primitives, and an execution environment from a single visual human demonstration, generating object‑centric relational programs that transfer to a real Franka arm across eight contact‑rich tasks and LIBERO‑Pro benchmarks.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparisons are provided, leaving performance relative to prior methods unclear.

## HomeBody: VLM‑driven Humanoid with Spatial Tool Calls

### The Breakthrough
HomeBody lets a vision‑language model output a skill name and spatial target (e.g., image point or map coordinate) which a tool call turns into a full motion pipeline using segmentation, Fast‑FoundationStereo depth, analytic grasp calculation and spline‑based planners, demonstrated on picking, navigation, placing and drawer‑opening.

### The Caveats
The post provides no quantitative or hardware results beyond the authors' own demo.

## Stripe Patterns Fool AI‑Powered Vehicles and Robots

### The Breakthrough
UF researchers showed that black‑and‑white stripe patterns corrupt stereo depth estimation, causing false distance readings, and introduced a lightweight software filter plus model modifications that reduce erroneous predictions on both simulation and a real autonomous‑vehicle test platform.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no baseline comparisons, so robustness improvements are unverified.

## OpenAI Codex Agents Bug Costs $78k

### The Breakthrough
A single Codex request in version 0.144.0‑alpha.4 spawned 826 child agents, consuming ~2.1 trillion tokens (~$78 k) due to a bug that inflated per‑child token usage to 264 M versus 31 M in later builds.

### The Caveats
The incident relies on one user’s anecdotal logs with no server‑side verification or independent replication.

## Synaptic Harmony: Multi‑Agent Q‑Learning Swarm Foraging Simulation

### The Breakthrough
The repository provides a Python/NumPy sandbox where each forager maintains its own Q‑table in a dynamic grid world with renewable resources and moving obstacles, fully configurable via YAML and visualized in real time.

### The Caveats
No quantitative evaluation or baseline comparison to existing multi‑agent RL methods is provided.

### Priority
AD‑WM shows how modest architectural tweaks can turn learned world models into practical planners that dramatically boost real‑world pick‑and‑place success, making it the most immediately impactful advance for robotics today.

### One action
Consider adding an action‑recovery regularizer to your latent dynamics model to improve MPC performance.
